before: Tracked automation edits that touched another author's pending text revision refused, a single decision on a nested text revision refused, and a tracked insertion inside another author's insertion nested inside it.
after: Outside a collaboration session, tracked automation edits nest a deletion in another author's pending insertion and place new words beside deleted text. In a session, the editing API refuses strikes and new words inside another author's pending insertion and new words right after it, and admits edits before it, strikes beside it, and new words after another author's deletion. A tracked insertion inside another author's insertion, from automation or page typing, splits their wrapper into two halves with the same revision identity when the wrapper is the direct parent, and refuses inside a link or content control within it. A single decision resolves a nested text revision's own sites with the existing accept and reject operations.
reason: No new operation, field, or format is added. The split writes two ordinary insertion wrappers that share one revision identity, a structure released readers already read. Released writers still nest, which released and new readers also understand. The edits and decisions reuse the deleteText, insertText, acceptRevision, and rejectRevision operations. Residual risk, unchanged from released clients: shared text keeps a wrapper as a character attribute, so a concurrent accept or reject of an insertion and an edit inside it or right after it can lose the decision, move a following character into the insertion, or reorder the new characters (#1354, #1363). The editing API refuses those edits in a session. Page typing in suggesting mode keeps the released exposure: nesting and splitting behave the same under that race.
